text:
Gabriel Landeskog won the Masterton and the Messier Leadership Award last season for coming back from years of knee trouble, and this season he looks like a hockey player again rather than a comeback story. Eight goals in 21 games, two of them in Toronto on Nov. 10, and a new line with Nazem Kadri and Nicolas Roy that The Denver Post and Sportsnet both wrote up after that game.

His minutes are modest, about 15 a night, and his shooting (26.7%) is running far ahead of what anyone sustains. But the goals have mattered: he ranks 35th in the league in our wins added, which credits goals by how much they swing a game. And his line has scored 5.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve, so his points have been held back too.

Evan Rawal of the Denver Gazette noted that his five-on-five shot generation started slowly and was climbing back. That's the thing to watch. Evolving-Hockey points out he plays with very strong teammates, which flatters the raw numbers. Still, the captain is scoring, the Avs have won six of ten, and that's a good sign for Colorado.
